Against a from-source reconstruction of that chain BLME agrees 24/24 (8 seeds x k = 5/10/14, 200 points in 6 dimensions) under the reference's own k convention, which I re-verified directly: NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=4).kneighbors_graph(X) returns row sums of exactly 4 with all 50 diagonal entries set, so the reference's nominal k INCLUDES self and maps to k_BLME = k_ref - 1. It reproduces the published number: Naitzat Fig. 3(e)'s hollow torus (published beta = (1,2,1)) reads (1, 2) at N = 1000 AND at N = 2000. MY OWN ROUND-5 YELLOW IS CLOSED: the task is now wired to a layers[-1] forward hook and emits _meta_last_entry_is_block_output, which read True on both models I ran end to end at the shipped config, and gpt2's numbers moved to exactly the values I predicted from the true block output -- h1_max_persistence 0.111111 -> 0.14285714285714285, h1_max_persistence_layer_frac 0.0 -> 1.0, h1_total_persistence_mean 10.998 -> 12.808792449881835. I ALSO REFUTE round-5 codex's remaining YELLOW item by measurement. Its duplicate-tie counterexample reproduces (12 points, 6 of them duplicated, k=2: the self index survives in the retained columns for 4 of 12 rows and H1 max/total read 0.16666667), but it is unreachable twice over: the RELEASED reference de-duplicates the cloud before building the graph (betti_calc.py read_csv does np.unique(..., axis=0)), so exact duplicates cannot arise in its protocol at all, and on the shipped LM path I measured 1000 unique rows of 1000 at gpt2 layers 0, 5 and 11 -- zero duplicates.
comparable_reason: Seven of the eight hard-Betti scalars carry no cross-model information at this protocol: on the two models I ran at the shipped N = 1000, beta_0 = 1 at all 18 layers, beta_1 = 0 at all 18, simplification_ratio = 1.0 on both, betti_0_decay_rate 9.18e-17 and 3.98e-17, max_betti_1 = 0 and max_betti_1_layer_frac = 0.0 on both. The continuous H1 family does vary but is not the quantity its name suggests: under the hop metric EVERY H1 bar has lifetime exactly 1 -- I measured the full barcode at gpt2 layers 0, 5 and 11 (130, 145 and 58 bars) and the set of distinct lifetimes is exactly {1.0} in all three -- so h1_max_persistence is identically 1/(hop diameter) and every one of gpt2's 12 emitted values is exactly 1/integer (1/9, 1/11, 1/19, 1/19, 1/17, 1/16, 1/15, 1/13, 1/12, 1/11, 1/9, 1/7). That makes it a graph-diameter statistic, and hop diameter grows with the cloud and with k, so it is not comparable across models or sample sizes as a persistence. On the two normalized variants: max_betti_1_layer_frac normalizes an argmax over a curve that is identically 0 (max_betti_1 = 0 on both models), so it is 0.0 on both by degeneracy rather than by measurement; h1_max_persistence_layer_frac is an argmax position over the 1/diameter curve and read 1.0 on gpt2 against 0.0 on pythia-70m -- it moves between the endpoints of the stack, and it FLIPPED 0.0 -> 1.0 on gpt2 from the post-final-norm hook alone. Neither carries a mechanism, hence normalized_ok RED.
github_reason: Read the released betti_calc.py and julia_include/julia_aux2.jl and rebuilt their chain from source (binary kneighbors_graph -> unweighted shortest_path -> classes alive at radius 2). The paper's per-layer D-I/D-II/D-III trajectories are not reproducible here because they are computed per CLASS MANIFOLD on labelled synthetic data (2,600-11,250 points each), which the LM adaptation does not have.
confounds_reason: The paper-defined outputs cannot be confounded because they are CONSTANT on the panel (beta_0 = 1 and beta_1 = 0 at every layer of both models, simplification_ratio = 1.0). The continuous family is a hop-diameter proxy by the measurement above (every value exactly 1/integer, lifetimes all exactly 1), and hop diameter depends on N and k rather than on model capability, so a cross-model ranking of h1_max_persistence would largely rank graph diameters. I did not have enough varying panel values to estimate a rho against d_model or n_layers, hence SUSPECTED rather than CONFIRMED.
